page_title: Graph-Level Prediction and Inductive Capability of GCNs
summary: This lecture page explores the inductive capability of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), focusing on their ability to generalize to new nodes and graphs of varying sizes. It details methods for graph-level prediction, specifically how to combine node embeddings into a single graph representation using global pooling techniques like mean, max, and sum. The content also introduces hierarchical pooling (DiffPool) as a method to better differentiate graph structures and discusses the importance of parameter sharing for efficient learning across different graph topologies.

parsed.page_title: Graph-Level Prediction and Inductive Capability of GCNs
parsed.summary: This lecture page explores the inductive capability of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), focusing on their ability to generalize to new nodes and graphs of varying sizes. It details methods for graph-level prediction, specifically how to combine node embeddings into a single graph representation using global pooling techniques like mean, max, and sum. The content also introduces hierarchical pooling (DiffPool) as a method to better differentiate graph structures and discusses the importance of parameter sharing for efficient learning across different graph topologies.
